hints: Focus on what happens to the added $OH^-$ ions in W and X, does one metal hydroxide stay dissolved while the other forms a solid?
Recall that $Mg(OH)_2$ is sparingly soluble and precipitates, while $Ba(OH)_2$ is soluble, so free $OH^-$ is removed only in X.
For Y and Z, compare sulfate solubilities to decide which mixture gives an insoluble $MSO_4$ precipitate and therefore the greater mass.
walkthrough:
**Work out the starting moles**

All four tubes start with the same amount of salt. Each has $25 \text{ cm}^3$ of $0.1 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ solution.

Moles calculation:
$$n = c \times V = 0.1 \times \frac{25}{1000} = 0.0025 \text{ mol}$$

**Compare W and X with NaOH**

Both get the same $0.0025 \text{ mol}$ of $NaOH$, so the same $0.0025 \text{ mol}$ of $OH^-$ is added.

Reactions to consider:
$$Ba^{2+} + 2OH^- \rightarrow Ba(OH)_2(aq) \text{ soluble}$$
$$Mg^{2+} + 2OH^- \rightarrow Mg(OH)_2(s) \text{ precipitate}$$

**Decide the higher pH**

In W, the $OH^-$ stays in solution because barium hydroxide is soluble. The liquid stays strongly alkaline.

In X, $OH^-$ is used up to form solid $Mg(OH)_2$, so free $OH^-$ concentration falls. Lower $OH^-$ means lower pH. Therefore W has the higher pH.

**Compare Y and Z with H2SO4**

Both get $0.0025 \text{ mol}$ of $H_2SO_4$, so $0.0025 \text{ mol}$ of $SO_4^{2-}$ is added.

Reactions to consider:
$$Ba^{2+} + SO_4^{2-} \rightarrow BaSO_4(s) \text{ insoluble}$$
$$Mg^{2+} + SO_4^{2-} \rightarrow MgSO_4(aq) \text{ soluble}$$

**Decide the greater mass of precipitate**

In Y, insoluble white $BaSO_4$ precipitates in good yield. In Z, magnesium sulfate is soluble so essentially no precipitate forms. Therefore Y has the greater mass of precipitate. Together this gives W and Y.

options.A: Correct. W keeps its $OH^-$ in solution so pH stays high, while X loses $OH^-$ as $Mg(OH)_2(s)$. Y forms insoluble $BaSO_4(s)$, while Z forms soluble $MgSO_4(aq)$, so Y gives the greater precipitate mass.
options.B: Half correct but half wrong. W does have the higher pH, but Z does not give more precipitate. $MgSO_4$ is soluble, so Z gives almost no solid while Y gives $BaSO_4(s)$.
options.C: Half correct but half wrong. Y does give the greater precipitate, but X does not have the higher pH. Students choosing X forget that precipitation of $Mg(OH)_2$ removes $OH^-$ and lowers the pH.
options.D: Both parts wrong. X has lower pH because $OH^-$ is consumed, and Z has almost no precipitate because $MgSO_4$ is soluble. This choice reverses both solubility trends for magnesium versus barium.
